args.envNote: There is no Docker in v3 (the operator's ruling of 2026-10-19). The local server in this container is SQL Server 2022 Express installed natively, a sqlservr process of the mssql user on 127.0.0.1,11434; its SA password is in ~/.dbchange/sql.env, which the fixture tests read (never print it). Since 1f2a47e every DacFx plan and publish goes through io/DacFx.Scripted, which gives DacFx script paths in a folder made for each call, because DacFx's own temp-file naming lets two concurrent calls on one database name lose a script on Windows. v2's own CI lanes under .github/workflows/ (ssdt-agent-*, analyzers, verifiability, lint) are the archive's oracle: never edit them. wps.title: WP 3.8 completed: the planter's plan with its last review findings fixed
wps.brief: WP 3.8 of V3_MILESTONES.md (§9), kernel Witness, the existing-data tier's plan ported test-first from the Facsimile's archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/cases/20-planter.md, was built in wave 5 and reviewed through two fix rounds; its latest branch is wp/3.8-r2. It did not converge on four should-fix findings, no must-fix: they are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/specs/wave5-3.8-open.txt, among them Repeats counting planted NULLs as repeated values of a unique key (a filtered index's NULLs never collide; an unfiltered unique index admits one NULL, so the need is named by that cause), Room returning long.MaxValue into a need's message, a property test that accepts any need where it should name which, and DECISIONS.md lines 145 to 150 to be tightened. Create your branch from the base, merge wp/3.8-r2 into it (resolving any conflict with the base's later commits), then fix each finding with a test that would fail without the fix. The original brief, which still holds: from the copy's Schema and Order (kernel/Schema*.cs, kernel/Order.cs), the preconditions and an ExistingData (kernel/Preconditions.cs), the rows to plant table by table: one valid row where the environment has rows, with its NOT NULL foreign-key ancestors (an ancestor reuses a seeded row first); one violating row per precondition answered violating, per value or collation class; per table the largest of its needs, not their sum; a child linked to a planted or seeded parent wherever the change validates a foreign key; values in nullable columns so a populated clean table stays clean; ordinal literals fitted to each column's width, with no Random, no clock, no seed and nothing from an environment; a few presence rows per table without an ExistingData; planter-needs-row named where ordinal literals cannot satisfy a check. Done when: every pure case of cases/20-planter.md for the six kinds passes with its case identifier; two plans from the same inputs are identical (D1); a schema edit changes only the touched tables' rows (D3); and V3_PARITY.md PAR-032 and VALUES.md's planted forms of D6, P1, P2 and P3 name the tests. Per-file budget: 500 lines a code file, 140 characters a line.

Create your branch from the base and merge wp/S9-11 into it. The base gained wave 5's H5 and WP 2.2 since: expect conflicts in NEXT.md (keep H5's text and add only what S9-11 changes about next steps), DECISIONS.md (keep both, in date order), V3_PARITY.md (§0's tally is whatever ParityResolves prints after the merge; keep both sides' row changes), and V3_MILESTONES.md (keep both; stay within its manifest budget). The spikes' original brief: S9, a schema read keeps a disabled check and foreign key, and untrusted only as the annotation IsNotTrustedPropertyAnnotation, so WP 3.5's trust step reads is_disabled and is_not_trusted from the catalog; S10, constraint validation runs after the commit and the whole post-deploy script on both releases; S11, system-named constraints differ by name between copy and environment and the head plans agree once names are replaced by their roles; each a fixture test, the 170.5.96 half in process and the 162.5.57 half through tests/DacFx162/; and check drift names a check written with IN with its remedy, exit 5 unchanged, law 2′ unchanged (the operator's ruling of 2026-10-19). Done when: both lanes are green with the exact counts reported, V3_PARITY.md's rows that name the receipts resolve, and V3_MILESTONES.md §6's S9 to S11 rows point to the receipts.

wps.title: io/LocalServer completed, and spike S4 timing a copy's create, publish, backup, restore and drop
wps.brief: Complete WP 3.4 of V3_MILESTONES.md (§9) and run spike S4 (§6). A scout mapped what exists: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/specs/3-spike-s4-wp-3-4-io-localserver-compl.json; since then the operator ruled (DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20): no Docker anywhere in v3; io starts no server and chooses DBCHANGE_SQL, then the SQL Server ~/.dbchange/sql.env names, then LocalDB, a missing one being exit 4 naming ci/sql.sh up or ci/sql.ps1 up; and a server is accepted when its major version is at least the package's platform. Those landed in wave 2. What remains: the first connect retried once; the sweep, which drops only this host's registered copies older than a day so that a killed run's copy is swept by the next (move the clock through a parameter, since io may not read the clock in a way tests cannot drive); backup and restore into the copy cache, where a backup can only land where the server process can write: LocalDB runs as the caller, so .dbchange/cache/ works; the native SQL Server runs as the mssql user, so back up to its instance default backup path (SERVERPROPERTY('InstanceDefaultBackupPath')) and record the file there in .dbchange/cache/'s index; a DBCHANGE_SQL server on another machine has no cache, and the base is published from scratch with a note saying so; two concurrent runs share nothing; and the environments file's unread localServer key, which NEXT.md says WP 3.4 drops, dropped from kernel/Environments.cs, tests/Golden/dbchange/environments.json and the tests that name it. Spike S4: a fixture test that times CREATE, publish, BACKUP, RESTORE and DROP of a copy of a 300-table schema (generate it in the test from the golden project's shapes) and prints each timing in the test output without asserting on time; it runs on both CI operating systems (the native server on Ubuntu, LocalDB 17.0 on Windows). Its answer, whether a fresh copy for a proof is a restore or a publish from scratch, becomes a decision line once CI's timings are read, which the parent session records; your notes give the local timings. Done when: two concurrent runs share nothing; a killed run is swept by the next; a backup restores into a copy equal to its base (the empty plan); S4's test prints its timings. Safety: a copy is made only through the registry; the sweep drops only registered names of this host; nothing touches a database the registry does not hold. Per-file budget: 500 lines a code file, 140 characters a line.
